cycles.summary: Corrected child credit points from a flat 1.0/child (+1.5 mother under-5) to the real age-banded table (birth year 2.5, ages 1-2 4.5, age 3 3.5, ages 4-5 2.5, ages 6-17 2 mother/1 father, age 18 0.5 mother). The old values understated parents' credits by 1-3.5 points/child, overstating their tax.
lessons: Child credit points are age-banded AND parent-asymmetric (6-17 is 2 for the mother, 1 for the father); a flat per-child figure is materially wrong, not conservative.

Fixed the reference file, the script comment, and avoided picking between the §1 (13,566) and §2 (13,769) average-wage variants, which are both real BTL figures used for different purposes.

Reconciled by stating both in the body + evidence: 6% is the mandatory minimum; 8.33% is the full Section 14 arrangement that discharges statutory severance liability. Calculator keeps 6% (correct default).

cycles.trigger: Remediation: the bundled script could not reach the skill's own rate table, and that table was itself incomplete against the official source.
lessons: A reference table that code cannot select from is not coverage. The skill documented a six-row Bituach Leumi category table while scripts/calculate_payroll.py hardcoded one row, so every non-standard employee was silently quoted the standard rate. The fix is the --ni-category dimension plus a domain-checklist row that makes reachability-from-code part of the coverage test.

Re-render the official table rather than trusting a prior cycle's transcription. Two defects only surfaced from a fresh extraction: the 67-to-70 row is women AND men (the skill said men), and its reduced-tier National Insurance component is 0.70% (the skill said 0.61%, which did not add up with the 3.23% health rate to the row's own published 3.93% total).

A correct rate can carry an unsourced label. The 3.23% / 5.17% disability row was right, but the '75%+/100%' qualifier attached to it was nowhere on the cited page; the official label is a work-injury or general-disability pension with an annual Bituach Leumi confirmation.

btl.gov.il rate pages serve real table markup to a plain curl. Extracting the <table> rows is both faster and more reliable than WebFetch, which had returned contradictory employee rates on this page in prior cycles.

lessons: CORRECTNESS (temporal): the skill dated Amendment 252 to January 2026 and printed 3.5% / 12.0% as '2025 values'. BTL's own table dates the 1.04% / 4.51% / 3.23% rates from 01.01.2025 and 5.17% from 01.02.2025, and ICPAS's tax-year-2025 tables show the same rates with thresholds 7,522 / 50,695. Every prior cycle verified the 2026 numbers as correct, which they are; none asked which year they started in. The evidence snippet itself said 'החל ב- 01.01.2025' while the claim beside it said 2026.

COVERAGE (3g cross-check): kamaneto.com matched the script to the shekel at 8k-20k and for a minor, but diverged 5.4% at 70k because it imputes employer pension deposits above 7.5% x 34,423 and severance above 3,798/month as taxable income. The script now does this. A cross-check limited to 'typical' salaries would never have found it: always include a high earner above 2.5x the average wage.
CARRY RESOLVED: keren hishtalmut is now in the script (--keren-hishtalmut), deposited on salary up to the 15,712 exempt ceiling, which is what kamaneto models too.

PANEL ROUND 1 (Expert, verified by author at BTL): imputed employer deposits above the exempt ceiling ARE liable to NI and health (BTL circular 1460 / employers 1479, item 5, 'הפרשות המעסיק מעבר לתקרה - חייבות בזקיפת שווי'). The first draft left them out and called the question 'unsettled' instead of looking. With the fix the script matches the Malam/Synerion NeoPay engine to the agora on all 30 of the Expert's cases (keren via the new --keren-full-salary, which is Malam's convention; kamaneto caps at 15,712).

CRITICAL, pre-existing since before v1.3: credit-points.md granted 2 points for 'Disabled' and 'Blind'. The Ordinance gives a s.9(5) EXEMPTION (blind, 100% or 90%+ weighted; 684,000 / 81,960 ceilings 2024-2027) and nothing to other disabled employees. Also wrong for years: the s.37 spouse point (only a 'יחיד מוטב'), vocational '0.5 tier' (s.40D has none), BA deferral (2014-2022 text only), settlement 'points' (s.11 is a percentage credit). Missing: s.40B working-youth point. Read the Ordinance (he.wikisource raw) for every credit row; secondary guides got four of these wrong.

Deferred (Expert minor): employer-paid disability insurance (אכ"ע) inside the 7.5% tagmulim exemption is not an input, so imputation is understated for bituach menahalim employees. Hourly minimum 35.40 vs BTL's 34.64 on a 186-hour divisor: kolzchut's 35.40 kept.

Checker net-salary: in addition to the 70k case, every golden case between ~39,700 and 51,910 gross now differs (NI on the imputed excess), and its credit inputs lack the 16-17 youth point. Regenerate in Phase 9.2.

PANEL ROUND 2 (Expert iteration 2): the round-1 repair INTRODUCED two defects. (1) It gave every 100%/90% disabled employee the s.9(5)(א) 684,000 ceiling; the text limits (א) to monthly-benefit recipients under the Invalids Law or the Hostile Action Victims Law, and everyone else, including a blind person without such a benefit, falls under (א1): 445,200, with 90% requiring 40% from one impairment. Reading s.9(5) in full, not the sentence found by search, would have caught it. (2) --keren-full-salary was cited alone in the SKILL text but did nothing without --keren-hishtalmut; it now implies it. Judge the repair, not only the original.

PANEL ROUND 3 (Judge + Expert): the round-2 text applied the 100%/90%/40% tests to the blind too. In s.9(5) the percentage clause follows 'נכה' only; blindness qualifies by itself on either route. Kol-Zchut (blindness certificate, no medical committee) was unreachable (403/redirect) this cycle, so the fix rests on the statute text alone.
